newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes astronaut Lucid back to Earth.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes astronaut Lucid back to Earth.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday welcomed astronaut Shannon Lucid back to Earth after a record 188 days in space, marvelling at her "amazing achievement."

"There's so many things to say about the incredible skill and stamina and dedication it takes to be in space for six months ... It's a monument to the human spirit," said Clinton, in Texas on a re-election campaign trip.

Dressed in a blue flight uniform, the 53-year-old Lucid, who returned on Thursday, looked a little unsteady on her feet as she walked to the podium for the official greeting outside the NASA hangar at Ellington Air Force Base.
Lucid was with the crew of the shuttle Atlantis that picked her up from the Russian space station Mir where she set records for the longest time in space by a woman and an American.

Atlantis landed at Kennedy Space Centre in Florida on Thursday morning. Despite spending six months in a weightless environment, Lucid managed to walk off the shuttle thanks to a grueling exercise regimen aboard Mir.
She was originally scheduled to return to Earth in August but her stay was extended for six weeks when the shuttle was grounded for mechanical problems and two hurricanes.

"I think we all feel at least that we've gotten to know Dr. Lucid, watching her grin and bear it as the mission was extended, hearing her eagerness to see her family, her yearning for what she called 'the wind in the sun,'" Clinton said.

"Perhaps more than she knows, she has also set a remarkable example for a new generation of young Americans and especially young girls all across this country who look up at her and see new possibilities for themselves," he said.
Clinton said Lucid's mission "continues to cement the close and growing bonds" between the U.S. and Russian space programmes.
